en-US.description:
Ten pieces. That is all Cinch needs before it can dress you.

Photograph ten things you already own — three tops, two bottoms, a dress, two pairs of shoes, a coat and a bag. Don't wear dresses? Cinch turns that position into another top or bottom. It identifies each piece, counts what your ten can make, and dresses you in the first outfit.

You do not have to photograph your whole wardrobe first. Ten pieces is a wardrobe, and the ten-piece closet is free.

BUILT FROM WHAT YOU OWN
Every outfit is assembled from garments in your closet. Cinch does not invent a missing piece or ask you to buy one first. Use your own photograph, or choose a shop's product image for something you already own.

YOUR CLOSET FIRST
Shop only when something is genuinely missing. Cinch can show up to three retailer options for a named closet gap, or open the shop page for a piece in a friend's closet. Cinch has no cart or checkout. Some links may earn commission; a paid link is labelled on the link itself.

THE MATHS RUNS ON YOUR PHONE
Outfits are built and scored on your iPhone from your real garments, so Cinch still dresses you on a plane or with no signal. Colour is judged in OKLCH, a perceptual colour space. Weather, formality, plans, wear history and your reactions shape the result. A model may re-rank a short list the on-device engine already built and write the reason underneath; it cannot add a garment that is not in that list.

EVERY OUTFIT COMES WITH ITS REASON
Not a score or percentage — a sentence explaining why this coat, on this day, over this knit.

DRESSED FOR THE ACTUAL WEATHER
Cinch uses apparent temperature where you are, not only the forecast high. It accounts for wind and rain, and avoids rain-hostile materials.

IT UNDERSTANDS A WHOLE DAY
Dinner at seven and drinks at ten are not the same dress code. Type what is ahead, or optionally connect your calendar, and Cinch looks for one outfit that carries the day.

IT LEARNS YOU
Like an outfit, skip it, or say why it is wrong — too formal, not your colours, worn too recently. Cinch adjusts from your reactions and shows what it has learned.

PACK WITHOUT OVERPACKING
Tell Cinch where you are going and for how long. It reads the forecast there and works out a small set of clothes that can cover the trip, while saying plainly when a day cannot be filled.

ASK THE STYLIST
Ask what to wear or what your closet is missing. The stylist answers from what you own and says when the right thing is not there.

ASK YOUR FRIENDS
Create an invite-only event, share options from your closets, vote and comment. Browse a friend's shared closet and privately ask to borrow a piece. Blocking and reporting controls are built into the social surfaces.

SEE YOUR OWN STORY
Cinch records wears, most-worn and untouched pieces, and cost per wear. Storage is reversible and keeps the photograph and wear history. Permanent removal is a separate, confirmed action.

PRIVATE BY DEFAULT
iOS gives Cinch only the photos you choose. Cinch asks before a garment photo is sent for AI identification. Typed garment descriptions search Datafeedr's licensed catalogue without being read by an AI model; a separate photo-based brand search runs only when you ask. There is no advertising and no tracking across other apps. Your closet stays private until you share it, and you can delete your account and its data inside the app.

Terms of Use: https://cinchstyle.com/terms

en-US.whatsNew: The stylist's doors now wear your own clothes. Compose your own outfit for the day — your pieces, your call, logged to your diary. Explore gains quick doors to your people and, at the end, pieces from the shops like the ones you already own. Plus cleaner spacing in the closet, a smoother sign-in, and a proper reveal for closets that never got theirs.

review.notes:
SIGNING IN
Cinch has no passwords. Tap "Sign in with Apple" and use any Apple ID; no invite code is required. The email option sends a six-digit code to the address entered. Leave the Demo Account fields empty.

FIRST RUN
A new account is walked through adding ten pieces. The photo library is the fastest review path; any ten clothing images will do. Describe is also available. After tagging, The Reveal shows the computed outfit count and first outfit.

LISTING PHOTOS AND SHOP LINKS
Describe searches Datafeedr's licensed catalogue and offers up to six product images; no AI model reads the typed description. Pasting a product URL reads that page's image for confirmation. "Find the listing photo" on an already-photographed piece sends that photo for a brand search only after the user asks and consents. Nothing is saved without the user choosing an image. Removing a listing photo restores the user's original photograph.

Cinch may open an external retailer page from a named closet gap, a piece in a friend's closet, or the Explore tab's "Like your closet, from the shops" shelf — a licensed-catalogue browse of the garment kinds the user already owns (category names only are sent; nothing typed and no closet content). The shelf disappears entirely when "Show where to buy" is turned off in Privacy & data. It has no cart or checkout. A link can earn affiliate commission only for a confirmed merchant relationship, and any paid link is labelled on the link itself.

SUBSCRIPTIONS
The app grants 14 days of full access on first launch. This is an app-side grant, not a StoreKit introductory offer, so no purchase or sandbox trial is required to evaluate the app. The paywall is dismissible. After the grant, the free tier remains usable.

Auto-renewing subscriptions:
Standard: $4.99/month or $39.99/year
Pro: $9.99/month or $79.99/year

The paywall appears after the first Reveal and at membership gates. Profile → Membership contains management and Restore Purchases. Terms and Privacy links are on the paywall.

SOCIAL FEATURES
Friends, events, voting, comments and borrowing require two accounts because all sharing is invite-only. To test: create an event from Plan, invite the second account, then share a look, vote and comment. Friends and borrowing are under Profile.

SAFETY CONTROLS
Blocking: any friend/profile row → ... → Block. Manage blocks at Profile → Blocked people.
Reporting: the ... menu on any shared look, comment or user profile. Event comments can be closed by the host; a locked board refuses further changes server-side.

PERMISSIONS
Camera, microphone, photo library, location, Calendar and notifications are requested only when their related feature is used. Location and Calendar are optional. Declining location uses the stated fallback city.

AI AND CATALOGUE PROCESSING
Garment photos can be sent through OpenRouter for identification after in-app consent. Typed garment descriptions use Datafeedr and reach no AI model. A separate photo-based brand search runs only on request. Outfit construction and scoring run on-device; a model may re-rank a shortlist and write its explanation. The Privacy page and https://cinchstyle.com/privacy disclose the processors and data categories.

ACCOUNT DELETION
Profile → Delete account. Deletion is immediate and removes uploaded photos, account data and social content.

CONTACT
hello@mail.cinchstyle.com

STYLE INSPIRATION, COMPOSE YOUR OWN, AND THE EXPLORE SHELF
The Stylist tab's second door is now titled "Style inspiration" (previously "Recreate a look"; same flow — a saved outfit photo rebuilt from the user's own closet).
NEW: "Compose your own" — under the Today tab's outfits, the user can pick any pieces from their closet and wear the combination today (it logs to their diary) or save it for later.
NEW: the Explore tab adds a doors row (Find people / Your circle / Invite) and, at the bottom, "Like your closet, from the shops" — product listings from the licensed Datafeedr catalogue for the garment CATEGORIES the user already owns (only fixed category words are sent; nothing typed, no closet content, no AI). Each card opens the merchant's own page; Cinch still has no cart or checkout. The shelf disappears when "Show where to buy" is off in Privacy & data, and does not render for an empty closet.
